newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Merrill Lynch cuts Hong Kong 96 inflation forecast.
newsitem.headline: Merrill Lynch cuts Hong Kong 96 inflation forecast.

text.p: Merrill Lynch said it revised its 1996 inflation forecast for Hong Kong down to 6.3 percent from 7.2 percent following a low inflation number in August.
The U.S. merchant bank also said Hong Kong may not have to raise interest rates, even if the United States hikes its short-term rates by 25 basis points.
"The benign inflation environment should preclude an interest rate rise in Hong Kong even if the U.S. raises rates by 25 basis points as expected," Merrill Lynch said.
Hong Kong pegs its dollar to the United States currency at a rate of HK$7.8 to US$1, which generally requires Hong Kong interest rates to move in step with U.S. rates.
The government on Monday said the increase in its consumer price index (A) moderated significantly in August to only 4.9 percent year-on-year, the lowest increase since July 1987.

Merrill Lynch said the downturn in inflation was largely due to a sharp deceleration in food prices to 1.5 percent during the month in review compared to an average rise of five percent during the first seven months.
"The easing inflation pressure should also raise real income further, underpinning our expectation of a consumer-led economic recovery," Merrill Lynch said. -- HK Newsroom (852)2843-6441
